close_reason: Fixed in bf895d2: documented the collision contract on ContactCard.extra, AddressBook.extra, and AddressBookRights.extra — programmatically inserting a key matching a typed field name produces a duplicate JSON key on serialize. RFC 8259 §4 leaves duplicate-key handling implementation-defined. Treat extra as a write-only catch-all for unknown keys discovered at deserialize.
description:
The diff adds `extra: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>` to
three structs with identical rustdoc:
- AddressBookRights (addressbook.rs:37)
- AddressBook       (addressbook.rs:81)
- ContactCard       (card.rs:185)

Rustdoc body:

> Catch-all for vendor / site / private extension fields not covered
> by the typed fields above. Preserves unknown fields across
> deserialize/serialize round-trip per workspace extras-preservation
> policy (see workspace AGENTS.md).

The rustdoc does not document **collision semantics**: what happens if
a caller programmatically inserts a key that matches a typed field?

```rust
let mut card = ContactCard::default();
card.name = Some(json!({"full": "Joe"}));
card.extra.insert("name".into(), json!("conflict"));
let wire = serde_json::to_string(&card).unwrap();
```

With `#[serde(flatten)]` on `extra`, serialize emits BOTH keys. JSON
permits duplicate keys (RFC 8259 §4) but downstream behavior is
implementation-defined:
- Most parsers take "last wins".
- Some parsers reject duplicates outright (strict mode, e.g.,
  serde_json's `--strict`, `denyUnknownFields`).
- Some parsers preserve both and emit a tuple/list.

A round-trip through serde_json itself takes "last wins" — the second
key replaces the first. So:

```rust
let back: ContactCard = serde_json::from_str(&wire).unwrap();
// back.name = ?
```

The outcome depends on field-emit order, which depends on serde's
struct-field iteration order. Empirically: the typed `name` field is
emitted FIRST (since serde processes named fields before flatten extras
in the struct definition order), so `extra["name"]` wins on round-trip,
silently OVERWRITING the typed value.

A defensive caller would have to write:

```rust
if !card.extra.contains_key("name") {
    card.extra.insert("name".into(), ...);
}
```

…on every insert. Forever. The workspace policy in AGENTS.md does not
document this.

Two acceptable resolutions:

1. Doc-only fix. Add a paragraph to the `extra` rustdoc on each affected
   struct:

   > Collision behavior: if `extra` contains a key matching a typed
   > field of this struct, serialization emits both keys (JSON allows
   > duplicates per RFC 8259 §4, but downstream parsers may take
   > last-wins, first-wins, or reject). Round-tripping through
   > serde_json takes last-wins, which means a key inserted into
   > `extra` overwrites the typed-field value on deserialize.
   > Callers MUST NOT insert into `extra` a key that names a typed
   > field of this struct.

2. Runtime safeguard. On serialize, return Err or panic if a typed-field
   key is present in `extra`. Cost: serde doesn't natively support this;
   would require a custom Serialize impl that drops the flatten
   attribute and walks fields manually. Heavy; not recommended.

Recommendation: option 1 (doc-only), plus a const list of known field
names in each module that a defensive caller can use to validate:

```rust
impl ContactCard {
    pub const KNOWN_FIELDS: &[&str] = &[
        "id", "addressBookIds", "version", "created", "kind",
        // ... all 22+ typed field wire names
    ];
}
```

This finding propagates: every struct in the workspace adopting the
extras-preservation pattern (per AGENTS.md §"Extras-preservation
policy") has the same doc gap. File a workspace-wide bead to sweep
the rustdoc clauses once the pattern is settled.

Cross-reference:
- AGENTS.md §"Extras-preservation policy for vendor/site fields"
- The propagation epic is bd JMAP-lbdy
- card.rs:184-185, addressbook.rs:80-81, addressbook.rs:36-37
title: extra Map collision with known field names is undocumented and produces duplicate JSON keys
